binds.giver: a lord who lost a battle of late

stages.journal: {giver} asks you to recover his house banner from the deserters who carried it off.
stages.canvas: A proud man asking for help with something that shames him: his banner, lost not to the enemy but to his own men who ran.
facts: After his last defeat, a band of his own soldiers deserted.
They took the house banner with them.
He wants it back; what becomes of them, he leaves to the player.

{giver}: After your last defeat a band of your own soldiers deserted and carried off your house banner. You want it back.

stages.journal: Find the deserters near {town} and take back the banner.

narration.canvas: After the fight, a wounded deserter speaks before the player, in the second person: not a plea, a grievance.
facts: Their captain was paid to hold the ford and fled with the silver before the battle.
They ran because they were left without orders or pay.
They took the banner so it would not be lost to the enemy.

stages.canvas: The banner returned. The lord's reaction to the deserters' tale is his own; he does not forget either.
facts: The banner is back in the lord's hands.
The deserters said their captain sold them out and fled with the silver.

{giver}: The player brings back your banner, and the deserters' tale: their captain took the silver and fled before the battle.

reward.memory: The player brought back my banner from the deserters, and with it a tale about their captain.

failure.memory: I asked the player to recover my banner; it is still lost.
